pain_points.description: The minimal worktree example shows `writes: [worktree_path, worktree_branch]` but no `contract:`. These fields are also listed under BaseState in §4. Unclear whether the worktree step needs to declare its own contract, or whether the harness implicitly supplies one for the create action. Guessed: omit contract, rely on framework-provided BaseState fields, and just list `writes:` as shown in the example.

Examples show `runtime: python` with `script:` and a default-runtime case with `command:`, but never explicitly state how to run multi-line shell commands. Pitfalls table mentions Bash auto-backgrounding but not how to declare a bash runtime. Guessed `runtime: bash` plus `command:` for the commit+push step.

It says `$`-substitution happens inside any YAML scalar string including `args:` and `cwd:`, but is silent on whether it applies inside `command:` strings. Inferred yes (since `command:` is a YAML scalar), and used `$state.worktree_path`, `$state.worktree_branch`, and `$inputs.ticket_id` directly in the command string.

The check example lists `on_fail: cancel | continue | retry_loop:<loop-id>`. Unclear whether `cancel` is exactly the spelling for the required behavior ("on reviewer FAIL, cancel the workflow"), vs. something like `abort` or `fail`. Took the literal token `cancel` from the example.

Unclear whether `merge_to_base` runs a git merge into the configured `base:` of the create step (here `main`) or whether it expects the branch to have been pushed first. The task said "on PASS commits and pushes the branch" then merge_to_base — not certain whether `merge_to_base` itself does any pushing. Went with: push explicitly, then call cleanup with merge_to_base for the local merge.

Two enum syntaxes appear (inline mapping `{ type: string, enum: [PASS, FAIL] }` in §5, full block form in §3 example 3). Both presumably work; picked the block form for review_status. Minor stylistic ambiguity, not a blocker.

The release-notes example uses `agent: claude` + `model: sonnet` but the "Required keys" table for `ai` only lists `prompt` and `contract`. Treated `agent`/`model` as optional and omitted them; loader should accept the defaults.

`allowed_tools:` shown only in the loop example and release-notes summarise step. Inferred it is a generic `ai` step key and used it on both implement-fix and review-diff. No explicit doc of the canonical tool names beyond the values shown (Read, Write, Edit, Bash).

self_assessment: I believe the workflow loads. It has the required 4 stages (worktree create → implement → review + check gate → commit/push + worktree cleanup), uses two standard prompts (implement.j2 and review.j2) with their documented required template_vars, declares contracts whose field names match `writes:` exactly, and uses the documented `worktree.create` / `worktree.cleanup` with `policy: merge_to_base`. The main residual risk is whether `runtime: bash` plus a multi-line `command:` is the right shape for the commit/push script step — AUTHORING.md doesn't show a bash-runtime example explicitly.
